children.name: Gracilechinus crepidarius
children.description: Six specimens examined, Annaba: wet weights 11.6 g, 15.12 g, and 21.8 g, diameter 3.8 cm, 5.6 cm, and 6.3 cm, height 2.4 cm, 4.6 cm, and 4.4 cm, respectively. Mostaganem: 106.5 g, 110.8 g, and 117.8 g, diameter 8.5 cm, 9.4 cm, and 10.8 cm, height 6.4 cm, 7.5 cm, and 7.9 cm, respectively. Body pentagonal, conical, circular contour, red with white stripes (Figure 5 A) flattened oral side (Figure 5 C). Meridian monochrome stripes often inconspicuous (Figure 5 D). Primary ambulacral tubercles present on each 2 plates (figure 5 D), numerous secondary ambulacral tubercles irregularly arranged. Large primary interambulacral tubercles present on every plate (figure 5 D), few secondary interambulacral tubercles above the ambitus, and more numerous and larger below. Spines sparse and few above ambitus, much more numerous and crowded on oral side, this spines of two sizes; primary spines long, reddish on the base, green and white on the apex. However, other variations are observed (Figure 5 A), secondary spines short; coloration varies from reddish to whitish (Figure 5 D). Numerous white ventral spines (Figure 5 C, 5 F). Generally, Gracilechinus acutus has the same appearance as Echinus melo Lamarck, 1816, and both species that have the same ecological niche are often confused. The main differences between the two species are as follows: a conical shape in Gracilechinus acutus, versus a spherical shape in E. melo; the test and spines of E.
